claim_audit: NAR March2026 median existing-home price$408,800 and FreddieMac April30,2026 thirty-year average6.30% are supported near publication. These are aggregate sold-home and qualifying-loan averages, not every buyer quote. Census available2024 household median$83,730 does not substantiate the script$86,185currentmedian; any alternative model/year needs identification. The specific520Klisting/78Kincome text-message story is unverified illustrative framing, not an observed underwriting case.

At408,800price,20%down and6.3%/30years, principal327,040 yields2,024.29monthly P&I. Reaching3Kall-in implies975.71monthly additional costs, but tax/insurance/maintenance assumptions are not itemized.3Kmonthly at28%gross implies128,571annualincome, broadly128K. The gap versus stated86,185 is42,386, not27K; using rounded128K gives41,815. Maintenance in the opening total is then absent from its later PITI/HOA/PMI28%test, so cash-flow definitions change.

NAHB January2021 original study uses2019AHS and estimates operating/maintenance costs near5%ofvalue, including taxes, fuel/utilities, insurance, upkeep and water/trash. Its maintenance component averages950/year, not5%ofvalue, and homesafter2010 totaloperatingratio around3%. The narration turns a combined operating estimate into closer-to5%maintenance alone, risking double-counting categories it separately adds. Roof/HVAC/appliance figures need local scope, service life and source; basic appliances start10K is unsupported as a universal minimum.

PWL/BenFelix5%rule is a heuristic built from property taxes, maintenance and cost of capital, with specific expectedreturn/borrowing/inflation assumptions. It is not a universal sum to which every full mortgage payment can be added. On500K at6%-7%, unrecoverable cost2,500-2,916.67monthly broadly reproduces, but moving the rule to6%-7% requires a consistent model, local rates, equity/debt mix and taxes. Rent is consumption cost and ownership includes unrecoverable costs; it is not literally only a hotel with toilet repair because equity, leverage, control and risk differ.

Homeowner/renter median net-worth gap is observational, not proof buying causes43xwealth. Age, income, selection and prior assets differ; SCF2022 owner396,200versusrenter/other10,400 in2022dollars differs from claimed430K/10K without a named updated source. Current median owners are not a counterfactual for current median renters. Seventy percent of this audience about to buy incorrectly is invented audience precision without analytics.

Closing2%-5%of400K=8K-20K is correct as a scenario; fee amounts, commissions, who pays, and broker/origination overlap vary. Inspectors/appraisers can be paid even if purchase does not close, contradicting none paid if you walk. Insurers receive premiums, not profit equal to every premium; lenders face default risk. Realtor/inspector duties, reputation and repeat business can align some interests, so only buyer loses is false. Mortgage securitization does not prove each displayed transaction follows the stated path.

Redfin March2026 source supports38buyersmarkets among50 and local negotiation differences; exact630Ksurplus is a dated estimate subject to revision, not guaranteed leverage on every home. Builder13.3%of450K=59,850 roughly60K, but matched Lennar period/source not recovered. First-year1.99buydown is not a permanent note rate; future payment, subsidy terms and qualification need the actual offer. Insurance46%/Florida7K/California17/Louisiana58/9%share lack matched releases here. Premiums rising20%-50%annually forever is not a supported forecast; compounding makes the absolute especially implausible.

Five-question checklist sensibly asks duration, reserves, payment burden, rent comparison and life stability.5-7years,3-6months and28/36% are planning heuristics, not guarantees or universal eligibility rules. Purchase/sale friction10%-15%is conditional on commissions, fees, tax and market; divorce41%/yearfive claim is unverified. Banks approve up to43% is not a universal statutory limit: CFPB GeneralQM amendment removed the43%DTI cap for that definition and replaced it with price-based thresholds. Lending programs/underwriting vary. PMIunder20%is a conventional-loan heuristic with exceptions; taxes/insurance/HOA and reserves remain expenses after fixed-rate P&I locks.

Price-to-rent cutoffs15/20/25 cannot establish buying clearly better without financing, tax, maintenance, expected appreciation, transaction timing, rent growth and opportunity returns. Comparable property quality and geography matter. SanJose45 earlier versus1.46M/(5,270x12)=23.09 later requires different property/data definitions, otherwise the example does not illustrate its earlierratio. Fixed-rate P&I can stay fixed while taxes/insurance rise; a30yearloan is not paid off after20years absent an explicit acceleration schedule. A mortgage can be refinanced/sold and is not a promise of30years predictable life.

Zia/Kent are illustrative, not verified observed people.85K/575K=14.78%down.490Kloan at6.3%/30years yields3,032.97P&I, not3,650 if the opening conventions apply; a different quote/term could explain but is omitted.4,800/(138K/12)=41.74%, broadly42%.575K/138K=4.17, not4.5timesincome. An85Ktotalcashbalance usedallfordown also leaves closingcosts unexplained.20%workhourdrop/600monthlygap,15Kpregnancycost and14monthdistress need income splits, insurance and budgets. Zeroreservesraisesrisk but doesnotguaranteeforeclosurein5months.

SanJose renter1.4Massets versus800Kequity after10years is not independently reproducible without investment return, home appreciation, loan amortization, closing/selling costs, taxes, cash reinvestment and rent/expense growth. The292Kdownpayment must be credited to the renter consistently. Gross diversified investments are not guaranteed liquid after-tax cash and house equity may be leveraged.600Kdifference is an unsupported scenario endpoint, not measured renter victory. Detroit24%cheaper and othercityratios/hottestHartford66%sourceperiods remain unverified; city lists do not replace a household ledger.

Historical real appreciation.4%-1.3% needs index, years, quality adjustment, rent yield and geography. Nominal5%versusreal1% are not directly comparable. Income/assets/cash are not interchangeable; loan principal is equity transfer, not all consumption loss, while appreciation can reverse. Tax deductions/itemization, sale treatment and local taxes can alter costs but are not universally available benefits. Invest difference aggressively is not risk-free or tailored to near-term home savings. ProjectedFedcuts/incentive/insurancechanges are forecasts, not guarantees; blanket sit tight for underwater owners omits household-specific alternatives and ongoing risks.
